AppIDs

The global catalog of AppIDs (billing key and access-control unit) and the binding of each server policy to exactly one AppID, fed by hand, by file upload or by a nightly URL import.

👤 ForAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage
📍 WhereGlobal ADOM → Administrator → AppIDs (URL /appids/)

What is it?#

An AppID is two things at once. It is a billing key: the customer a server policy is charged to. It is also an access-control unit: an API token can be pinned to AppIDs, so an external integrator only reaches the server policies bound to their AppIDs.

The AppIDs page manages the catalog and the bindings. Both live in SATOM's own database, never in a file or a policy comment. Files and URLs are only sources that feed the catalog.

What does it do?#

The page has four tabs:

  • Catalog: add an AppID by hand, see every AppID with its source and status (active, stale, inactive) and how many policies are bound to it, and delete one.
  • Upload & map: upload a CSV, TSV, TXT or PDF file, preview it, map its columns to fields once, and import. The mapping is saved and reused by later uploads and by the nightly import.
  • Nightly source: configure a URL (with optional basic or bearer authentication) that the scheduled action appid_import fetches.
  • Assign policies: bind a server policy on a device to an AppID, and remove bindings.

Imports are additive. They create new AppIDs and update existing ones, never delete anything, and never remove a binding. An imported AppID missing from the latest import is flagged stale (with the reason absent from feed on <date>). Hand-made (manual) AppIDs are never marked stale.

The catalog is global: one catalog for FortiWeb and FortiADC, and the device list on Assign policies contains both kinds of appliance.

Requirements#

  • For assignments: the appliance must be registered in SATOM and visible to you. Devices in maintenance mode are offered only if you hold appliances.view_maintenance. The server policy name is typed, not picked, so make sure it matches the policy name on the device exactly. For a FortiWeb, the policy must be in SATOM's local copy of the device configuration (last sync).
  • For PDF uploads: the server needs the pdfplumber package. Without it the preview answers PDF import needs the 'pdfplumber' package, which is not installed.
  • For the nightly import: a scheduled action of type Import AppID catalog (nightly) created under Scheduled actions. It is not created for you.

Permissions#

Every action on this page requires users.manage (Administrator). The Administrator menu group, and with it the AppIDs entry, is hidden from users without it. A direct request to /appids/ returns 403 Forbidden.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: the Assign policies device picker and the assign/unassign actions cover only the appliances visible to you, assigning a FortiWeb policy checks that the device has it, and unticking First row is a header now works.

The page is linked only from the Global ADOM. From the FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator consoles, the URL redirects to that console's home page.

How to use#

Add an AppID by hand#

  1. Open Administrator → AppIDs in the Global ADOM. The Catalog tab is shown.
  2. Fill AppID * and optionally Customer, Label and Rate.
  3. Click Add AppID. The flash reads AppID <id> created.

Import a catalog file#

  1. Open the Upload & map tab.
  2. Choose the File (.csv, .tsv, .txt or .pdf).
  3. Leave First row is a header ticked if the first row holds column names. Untick it for a file without a header row; columns are then referenced by index number and the first row is imported as data.
  4. Click Preview & map. The first rows appear in a table, together with any parser note (for example for PDFs).
  5. Under Map columns → fields, pick the AppID column * and, optionally, the Customer column, Label column and Rate column. Columns you saved previously are preselected.
  6. To keep more columns, click Add extra field, type a field name (for example environment) and pick its column. Repeat as needed.
  7. Click Import (additive). The flash reads Imported from <file>: <n> new, <n> updated, <n> newly stale, <n> skipped.

Configure the nightly source#

  1. Open the Nightly source tab.
  2. Set Source type to Fetch from URL (nightly) and enter the URL.
  3. Choose Auth: none, basic (fill Username (basic) and Password (basic)) or bearer (fill Bearer token).
  4. Click Save source. The flash reads External source + mapping saved. The nightly action will reuse it.
  5. Under Settings → System → System Automations, create an Import AppID catalog (nightly) action. It reuses the URL and the saved column mapping.

ℹ️Note

Do an upload with the same file layout first. The nightly import uses the column mapping saved by Import (additive). It does not ask for one.

Assign a server policy to an AppID#

  1. Open the Assign policies tab.
  2. Pick the AppID * and the Device *, and type the Server Policy name * exactly as it is on the device.
  3. Click Assign. The flash reads Policy <name> assigned. For a FortiWeb, a name that is not in SATOM's local copy of the device is refused (see Troubleshooting).
  4. If the policy was already bound to another AppID, the binding moves to the new one. A policy never has two AppIDs.

To remove a binding, click the × button on its row in the table below. The flash reads Policy <name> unassigned.

Delete an AppID#

  1. On the Catalog tab, click the trash button on the row.
  2. Confirm Delete AppID <id> and its <n> policy binding(s)?

The AppID and all its bindings are removed. The flash reads AppID <id> deleted (and its policy bindings).

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
AppID The key. Unique, compared case-insensitively Yes APP-1042
Customer Who is billed. Max. 200 characters No Example Corp
Label Free description. Max. 200 characters No Web shop
Rate Free text, max. 64 characters No 50
First row is a header Map columns by header name instead of position. Unticked: columns by index, first row is data — ticked
Extra field Name and column of any additional value kept per AppID No environment → Env
Source type Manual upload only or Fetch from URL (nightly) Yes Fetch from URL
URL Address the nightly import downloads For URL https://catalog.example.com/appids.csv
Auth none, basic or bearer Yes bearer
Password / Bearer token Stored encrypted. Leave empty to keep the stored value No —
Server Policy name Exact policy name on the device Yes pol-shop-example-com

Example#

🧪Example — Monthly billing file plus nightly refresh

Finance publishes appids.csv with the columns AppID;Client;Service;Price;Env. An admin uploads it once and maps AppID column → AppID, Customer column → Client, Label column → Service and Rate column → Price, and adds the extra field environment → Env. The import reports 120 new, 0 updated, 0 newly stale, 0 skipped. The admin then saves the same file's URL as the nightly source with a bearer token and creates the scheduled action. A week later one AppID disappears from the file. The next nightly run marks it stale, and its policy bindings and its billing link stay in place until somebody reviews it.

Result#

  • The catalog and bindings are stored in SATOM's database.
  • Each action writes an audit entry: appid.create, appid.delete, appid.import (with the counts), appid.source_save, appid.assign and appid.unassign.
  • An API token whose AppID scope lists AppIDs may only run backend, policy and certificate actions whose target server policy is bound to one of those AppIDs, and no fleet-wide action. Only bindings on appliances of the token's own product count.

Troubleshooting#

"No rows with a non-empty AppID were found — check the AppID column mapping."#

Possible causes - The AppID column points at the wrong column. - The file was mapped by header name, but the header changed.

Solution 1. Click Preview & map again and check the column names in the preview. 2. Pick the right AppID column and import again.

Verification - The success flash reports a non-zero new or updated count.

"AppID '' already exists"#

Possible causes - An AppID with the same key exists already, possibly in different upper or lower case.

Solution 1. Search the Catalog table for the key. Import a file instead if you want to update an existing entry. An import updates existing AppIDs.

Verification - The catalog shows exactly one row for the key.

A file without a header row loses its first line#

Possible causes - First row is a header was left ticked, so the first row was read as column names.

Solution 1. Untick First row is a header, click Preview & map, map the columns by index and import again. The saved mapping keeps the setting for the nightly import.

Verification - The import's new plus updated count equals the number of data rows.

" has no server policy named '' in the local store. …"#

Possible causes - The name is misspelt, or the policy was created on the FortiWeb after the last device sync.

Solution 1. Check the exact name on the device's Server Policy list. 2. If the policy is new, press Refresh from device on Server Policy and assign again.

Verification - The flash reads Policy <name> assigned.

The nightly action reports "AppID import skipped — no external URL source is configured (upload is manual-only)."#

Possible causes - Source type is still Manual upload only, or the URL is empty.

Solution 1. Open Nightly source, choose Fetch from URL (nightly), enter the URL and click Save source.

Verification - The next run reports AppID import: <n> new, <n> updated, ….

The nightly action reports "AppID import failed: …"#

Possible causes - The URL is unreachable, returned an HTTP error, or the credentials are wrong. - The file is a PDF and pdfplumber is missing.

Solution 1. Fetch the URL from the SATOM host with the same credentials. 2. Re-enter the password or token and click Save source.

Verification - The next run of the scheduled action reports a summary instead of an error.

Advanced#

Advanced Parsing, matching and storage
  • Delimited files are sniffed for ,, ;, tab and |. Ragged rows are padded. A PDF table is read page by page. A PDF without a table becomes a single text column, one line per row.
  • With a header, a mapping reference is matched by header name (case-insensitive), then by column index as a fallback.
  • An import never blanks a field: an empty cell keeps the stored value. Extra fields are merged into the AppID's existing extra values.
  • The mapping and source are stored in the application settings under appid.import.global. Password and token are Fernet-encrypted, and the page only shows whether one is set.
  • Bindings are unique per (appliance, server policy). The device picker lists only the FortiWeb and FortiADC appliances visible to you, and Assign and Unassign refuse an appliance outside that set.
  • For a FortiWeb, Assign checks the policy name against SATOM's local copy of the device configuration, not the live device. For a FortiADC, the name is not checked, and a misspelt name creates a binding that matches nothing.
  • The New Server Policy form can also bind the new policy to an AppID (administrators only); that binding is recorded as appid.assign too.
